title: HELM: Characterizing Unified Memory Accesses to Improve GPU Performance under Memory Oversubscription
problem: Unified Memory default migration policies severely degrade performance under memory oversubscription; existing solutions fail to generalize across applications
motivation: Characterize and predict UM access patterns to enable dynamic policy selection for improved performance under oversubscription
method: HELM collects data from the Unified Memory driver—the GPU's automatic memory-management system—to understand how programs access memory. By analyzing these access patterns, it determines which data should stay on the GPU and which can be moved back to main memory. HELM then uses this analysis to automatically select the data-migration policy that works best for each program, rather than applying a one-size-fits-all default.
key_novelty: HELM introduces metrics that reveal what programs actually do with GPU memory, enabling automatic optimization of data-migration policies and achieving an average 3.5x speedup.
contributions: Novel HELM metrics for UM access pattern characterization
Metrics derived from accessible UM driver telemetry for broad applicability
Methodology for policy selection under memory oversubscription
limitations: Evaluation limited to GPU unified memory; applicability to other memory hierarchies unclear; specific workload types not detailed
